newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Norway agree 1997 fish catch quotas.
newsitem.headline: EU, Norway agree 1997 fish catch quotas.

text.p: The European Union and Norway agreed on Wednesday, after three rounds of negotioations, fish catch quotas for 1997 jointly-managed North Sea stocks.
The deal paves the way for EU fisheries ministers to set fish quotas for member states when they meet on December 19-20.

"The agreement was adopted as a compromise package and is satisfactory," the European Commission said in a statement. "It will permit 1997 fishing activities only slightly below those available in 1996."
The EU will take 104,450 tonnes of cod and 88,780 tonnes of haddock out of total allowable catches (TACs) of 115,000 tonnes and 114,000 tonnes respectively.
It will also take 112,890 tonnes of herring and 16,950 tonnes of mackerel out of North Sea TACs of 159,000 tonnes and 52,755 tonnes respectively.
The EU and Norway also agreed a new framework for management of seriously-depleted North Sea herring stocks, including by-catches for animal feed and other industrial uses.
A July 1996 emergency halving of the North Sea herring allowable catch to protect threatened stocks will be extended through 1997.
Norway said in a statement that its fishermen would get 127,450 tonnes out of a total mackerel quota of 420,000 tonnes, which includes fishing grounds outside the North Sea.
It said that both sides had agreed to continue to cooperate in fisheries surveillance and to swap observers.
